authors/don.title: ᴅᴏɴ †
authors/don.content:
ᴅᴏɴ †

Self-improvement essayist publishing on Substack. Direct address, building each piece from a named mechanism — a cognitive bias, a neurochemical loop, a Japanese or Stoic philosophy, a figure from myth or history — toward a concrete practice. The recurring argument: potential is lost by default through consumption, excuses and inherited belief, and recovered deliberately through creation, incremental progress, and a curated internal world.

Website: nqdonzo.substack.com
Appears in: Psychology, Neuroscience & Self-Mastery
Sources in this wiki: 30
What they write about
16 recurring subjects across the 30 sources, each with the pieces that carry it.
Attention, consumption and the modern environment
Short-form video read as a variable-ratio reward schedule — the slot-machine comparison is explicit — plus the dopamine-spike to cortisol chain it runs, the attention economy stated as arithmetic (view → engagement → ad revenue), akrasia as the resulting loss of self-control, and the evolutionary-mismatch argument that hardware calibrated for scarcity is being fed abundance. Returns as doomscrolling in the habit lists, as Naval’s “the modern devil is cheap dopamine”, and as notifications stealing momentum.
In: The Consumption Dilemma · Remove These Five Destructive Habits That Are Destroying Your Potential · How to Destroy Your Potential in 90 Days · I’ll Make You Believe You Can Achieve Anything after Reading This · Read this If You Want to Cure Your Procrastination
Execution — starting, finishing, prioritising
Clarity and confidence as outputs of action rather than prerequisites for it (“the cold water won’t get any warmer if you jump late”), analysis paralysis, and procrastination given a cognitive-load account rather than a moral one: the brain’s energy budget, conscious bandwidth, state-dependent memory, the Zeigarnik effect, second-order consequence chains, and the outright denial of multitasking. The allocation half is the Pareto Principle with its provenance — Pareto 1906, Juran’s “vital few and trivial many” — used mainly in reverse, to name busywork.
In: The Execution Dilemma · Read this If You Want to Cure Your Procrastination · You Need a Mindset Shift on Priorities · Five Habits You Need to Implement Immediately
Excuses, inherited belief and identity
The recurring mechanism: an excuse is a neural pathway being myelinated until avoidance fires before conscious thought, and beliefs installed in childhood run as subconscious programs that awareness alone will not remove — evidence over months does. Named endpoints are learned helplessness, victim mentality and identity-based coping (“that’s just how things go for me”); the named antidote is an internal locus of control. Identity is treated as upstream of behaviour rather than downstream.
In: Discard These Excuses Immediately Before You Severely Cap Your Potential · Five Belief Systems You Need to Remove to Become Greater · Remove These Five Destructive Habits That Are Destroying Your Potential · How to Destroy Your Potential in 90 Days · I’ll Make You Believe You Can Achieve Anything after Reading This
Mental models and cognitive biases
Munger’s latticework — big ideas from the big disciplines, the man-with-a-hammer tendency, inversion, circle of competence, the map that is not the territory, the Lollapalooza effect, ignorance removal, second-order thinking — and the five biases marked for removal by the same two-step route: novelty bias and shiny object syndrome, loss aversion (worked through 2008), herd mentality and FOMO, Dunning–Kruger including its expert’s-doubt half, and overconfidence.
In: Why You Should Adopt Many Mental Models For Your Life · Rid Yourself of These Cognitive Biases so You Can Conquer · You Need a Mindset Shift on Priorities · How to Stop Wasting Your Life (and your time)
Compounding and incremental progress
Kaizen lifted out of manufacturing and applied to a person: small continuous steps, floors rather than ceilings, the bamboo’s invisible root years, Lucretius’ water wearing stone, 1% daily compounding to 37.7×, systems over goals, and the author’s own term “escape velocity” for the point where accumulated work converts into visible results. Hormozi’s “volume negates luck” is argued here and then qualified elsewhere — ten thousand kicks are worthless if they are subpar.
In: Kaizen: A Philosophy Every Creative Should Adopt · The Anatomy of Greatness: The Psychology of Being the Best · Five Crucial Lessons from the Human Embodiment of Self-Actualization: Bruce Lee · Nine More Timeless Lessons from Naval to Make You Greater
Greatness and what it costs
Greatness decomposed into traits — strong self-concept routed through ikigai, internal locus of control, intrinsic motivation, high agency, assiduity, delayed gratification tested by the marshmallow study — and then priced: trade-offs stated as non-optional, Kobe’s 3:30 AM, Jordan’s doubled work-rate becoming the team’s baseline, ego as the ceiling via Genghis Khan’s meritocracy. Why most people stop is answered statistically, with regression to the mean, and neurologically, with the path of least resistance myelinating until quitting is the identity. Environment, social circle (no yes-men), solitude as distinct from isolation, and Taleb’s antifragility are named as the inputs you actually control.
In: The Anatomy of Greatness: The Psychology of Being the Best · How You Can Reach Excellence in a World that Demands Lesser · How to Develop an Iron Mindset to Dominate · How to Develop Unwavering Confidence and Self-Belief
Burnout, recovery and the limits of optimisation
The counterweight to the rest of the corpus’s intensity: “are we chasing the vision, or the validation?”, the cortisol feedback loop of goal-attachment, monk mode reported as personal failure and busywork, Naval’s work-like-a-lion against grazing, rest between sets as what permits intensity, what neglected sleep costs through the glymphatic system, the law of diminishing returns against twelve-hour days, and a refusal to sacrifice your twenties for your thirties.
In: Forget “Locking In.” Sometimes You Need to Lock Out. · Five Belief Systems You Need to Remove to Become Greater · Kaizen: A Philosophy Every Creative Should Adopt
Habits, protocols and the neuroscience underneath
Five habits given with mechanisms — fasted morning runs (amygdala down, cortisol down, pain tolerance up), cold showers as a graduated Wim Hof protocol whose real yield is sitting with discomfort, journaling as “releasing internal tension by way of an external channel”, finishing what you start against a RAM-limited mind, and complimenting people, costed out in dopamine, oxytocin, serotonin and reward circuitry — against five to subtract: doomscrolling, broken promises to yourself, people-pleasing, vices, negative self-talk. Neuroplasticity and myelination are the engine in both directions, with ninety days as the point of permanence.
In: Five Habits You Need to Implement Immediately · Remove These Five Destructive Habits That Are Destroying Your Potential · How to Destroy Your Potential in 90 Days
Stoicism, non-attachment and the dichotomy of control
Marcus Aurelius through Meditations — the dichotomy of control, thoughts as the quality of life, the best revenge being not to be like your enemy, embodying rather than debating a philosophy, gratitude on waking — plus the distinction that carries a whole piece: detachment pushes a thought away and rehearses it (the pink elephant), non-attachment releases the claim on an outcome. Also Seneca and Epictetus’ premeditatio malorum, memento mori as a brake rather than a spur, and five Latin phrases read as portable dispositions.
In: How To Curate An Internal World So Unshakeable that Nothing Can Stop You · The Art of Non-Attachment (in Philosophy) · The Beauty of Latin Phrases: Five Powerful Sayings from Conquerors · How to Stop Wasting Your Life (and your time) · Modern Self-Help Books Isn’t Enough: Read History, Fiction, and Mythology
History, myth and the case against modern self-help
The industry sells shovels rather than gold, so read history, fiction and mythology instead — advice that survived harder conditions than ours. The recurring cast: Caesar weeping at Alexander’s statue, Diogenes telling Alexander to get out of his sunlight, Columbus anchoring his own status with an impossible ask, Hannibal crossing the Alps, Napoleon’s speed and then his Russia, Genghis Khan absorbing what he conquered, and Icarus read twice — flight worth dying for, and the pride that spent the altitude.
In: Modern Self-Help Books Isn’t Enough: Read History, Fiction, and Mythology · What You Can Learn from Icarus on Ambition · The Beauty of Latin Phrases: Five Powerful Sayings from Conquerors · The Anatomy of Greatness: The Psychology of Being the Best
Naval Ravikant’s framework
Eighteen lessons across two pieces: long-term games with long-term people, specific knowledge that cannot be taught or automated, desire as the fundamental delusion and happiness as the absence of wanting, the modern struggle as evolutionary mismatch, “save yourself” accountability, impatience with actions and patience with results, life lived in the arena rather than in theory — then inspiration as perishable, hard choices for an easy life, the optimistic contrarian, intelligence measured as getting what you want out of life, work that is play to you and work to others, and happiness as a trainable skill.
In: Nine Timeless Lessons from Naval To Make You Greater · Nine More Timeless Lessons from Naval to Make You Greater
Faith, self-belief and its calibration
Belief acted on before the evidence exists — Topuria’s faith placing the outcome outside himself, stated intention preceding the result, first-principles mastery of each discipline separately, Neville Goddard’s law of assumption qualified so it stays non-mystical, Muhammad Ali before Foreman — and the corpus’s own correction, since the same author later uses Topuria’s loss to Gaethje as the worked example of overconfidence bias. The tension between delusional optimism and staying close to objective reality is one the author names and does not resolve.
In: How to Develop Unwavering Confidence and Self-Belief · I’ll Make You Believe You Can Achieve Anything after Reading This · Rid Yourself of These Cognitive Biases so You Can Conquer · Remove These Five Destructive Habits That Are Destroying Your Potential
Other people — approval, boundaries and the circle
People-pleasing named as the single most destructive habit, boundaries as the highest form of self-respect, Aesop on pleasing all and Lao Tzu on being their prisoner, the ship that does not open holes to let water in. On the other side: an inner circle that tells uncomfortable truths instead of comforting lies, courage redefined for a digital era as indifference to judgment, authenticity traded for approval as the disease of the feed, and complimenting people against a norm that calls it glazing.
In: How to Destroy Your Potential in 90 Days · Remove These Five Destructive Habits That Are Destroying Your Potential · Five Belief Systems You Need to Remove to Become Greater · How You Can Reach Excellence in a World that Demands Lesser · Nine More Timeless Lessons from Naval to Make You Greater · The Consumption Dilemma
Meaning, purpose and finite time
Nietzsche’s why that makes any how bearable, Maslow’s self-actualization reached in Bruce Lee, the good life as a process rather than a state, and the paradox that meaning is generated by contrast — mapped to yin and yang, argued through cheat codes and frictionless goals. The urgency machinery is explicit: a vision and an anti-vision run together (the rat, the cheese, the cat), roughly 75 of each season, 109 billion people already dead, and time as the one commodity no amount of money buys back.
In: The Art of Perseverance · The Paradox of Life · Five Crucial Lessons from the Human Embodiment of Self-Actualization: Bruce Lee · How to Stop Wasting Your Life (and your time) · What You Can Learn from Icarus on Ambition
Neurodegeneration and protecting the brain
The longest piece in the corpus reads Everywhere at the End of Time against the actual pathology of Alzheimer’s — amyloid-beta plaques and tau tangles, hippocampal atrophy and ventricular expansion, retrogenesis, sundowning, aphasia decaying the album’s own cover titles, terminal lucidity in the final five minutes — and William Utermohlen’s self-portraits as the same decline in paint. The countermeasures are the point: sleep and glymphatic clearance, movement and BDNF, diet, and cognitive load heavy enough to keep synapses in use.
In: Everywhere at the End of Time: The Scariest Album Ever Created
The Genius Series
A recurring format rather than a subject: one figure studied per instalment — Charlie Munger (I), Naval Ravikant (II), Ilia Topuria (III), Michael Jordan (IV), Marcus Aurelius (V), Bruce Lee (VI) — each read for a transferable system rather than a biography.
In: Why You Should Adopt Many Mental Models For Your Life · Nine Timeless Lessons from Naval To Make You Greater · How to Develop Unwavering Confidence and Self-Belief · How to Develop an Iron Mindset to Dominate · How To Curate An Internal World So Unshakeable that Nothing Can Stop You · Five Crucial Lessons from the Human Embodiment of Self-Actualization: Bruce Lee

authors/ixcarus.title: ixcarus
authors/ixcarus.content:
ixcarus

Self-development writer publishing on Substack. The work blends neuroscience, evolutionary psychology, Jungian depth psychology, health optimization and social dynamics into a single claim: humans are biological machines running largely on autopilot, but the hardware can be reprogrammed.

Website: ixcarus.substack.com
Appears in: Psychology, Neuroscience & Self-Mastery
Sources in this wiki: 179
What they write about
25 recurring subjects across the 179 sources, each with the pieces that carry it.
Dopamine, wanting, and the economy of the baseline
Dopamine is treated throughout as the chemical of anticipation rather than pleasure — four pathways (mesolimbic, mesocortical, nigrostriatal, tuberoinfundibular), reward prediction error firing on the gap between expected and actual outcome, and a peak-versus-baseline economy in which artificial spikes buy height by lowering the floor toward anhedonia. Two inversions recur: “detox” is the wrong verb, because a system that kept ancestors alive for ten thousand years panics and finds worse replacements when starved, so the move is redirection into a need the low-value source was filling; and the wanting itself is not a defect but the engine of ambition, which is why work should be structured as a sequence of hunts where you never quite arrive. The downstream cases are the goal-achievement letdown, self-sabotage as the anticipation peak nearing its end, scarcity and reactance manufacturing desire unrelated to the value of the thing, the gym as a substitute that pays out visible progress while the harder invisible work starves, and delayed gratification framed as the one capability — with 98.2% never finishing what they start. Apathy is the floor of the same system: depleted baseline plus derealisation and dorsal-vagal shutdown, an empty quiet routinely mistaken for peace.
In: The Dopaminergic System: The Complete Neuroscience Breakdown · Your ‘Dopamine Problem’ Is Actually a Superpower · Why Your Dopamine Detox Is Failing · The Neuroscience of Desire (Why Wanting Feels Better Than Having) · Why You Always Want What You Can’t Have · The Four Chemicals That Control Your Happiness (And Why They’re Broken) · The One Ability That Separates Winners From Losers · Why Gym People Stay Poor (The Uncomfortable Truth) · The Psychology of Apathy
The attention economy and the engineered environment
Short-form video is the mechanism he returns to most, always described identically: the payout is the half-second of anticipation before the next clip loads, an eight-second variable-ratio schedule explicitly compared to a slot machine, with the threshold for “stimulating” recalibrating upward until real work and real conversation fall beneath it, and myelination making the damage structural rather than habitual. Around it sit Herbert Simon’s attention scarcity and the 1833 penny press as the origin of the you-are-the-product model, 47 videos watched and 3 remembered, the phone as most people’s primary emotional-regulation tool, screens as “digital cocaine” that leaves real life tasting like decaf, and consumption mistaken for progress — motivational content as “emotional porn” the brain cannot distinguish from succeeding. The prescribed antidote is boredom: receptor upregulation, the default mode network switching on, wall-staring before demanding work, walking without earphones. Two longer pieces move the argument from willpower to environment — algorithms supplying the predictions perception is built from (Plato’s cave, Bentham’s panopticon and Foucault’s internalised guard, Debord’s spectacle, the claim that ~90% of visual-cortex input comes from inside the brain), and trance as the brain’s factory setting, with infinite scroll defined as the deletion of the stopping cue and Costco and casino architecture as its physical-world equivalents. The reversal of the Flynn Effect is the population-scale version of the same claim.
In: What Short-Form Content Is Doing To Your Brain · Why 5 Second Videos Are Worse Than Drugs · The Attention Economy: You Are The Product · You’re Addicted and Don’t Even Know It · The Psychology Behind Phone Addiction · They Don’t Need To Cage You If You Cage Yourself: How Algorithms Are Constructing Your Reality · How You’re Killing Your Potential Without Realizing It · The Illusion Of Progress · Has The World Lost Its Color? · The Psychology of Consumerism: How Capitalism Needs You Miserable · The Neuroscience Of Hypnosis: How To Hijack The Exact Brain State Advertisers Use Against You · The Intelligence Decline Is Real. Here’s How To Go The Other Direction.
The subconscious as installed software
Between the third trimester and age seven the brain runs in theta — hypnotic absorption with no critical filter — so whatever went in during that window is still executing, in five named patterns: emotionally absent parent, conditional love, scarcity, unworthiness, hypervigilance. The subconscious is described not as a library but as a live predictive-processing machine that generates the emotional and physiological state before the event and then interprets reality through it, which is why “the knowing is conscious, the program is subconscious, and until you actually go in and update the program, the program wins.” Updating it takes felt experience rather than information, worked in the alpha/theta window twenty minutes either side of sleep; the crude Pavlovian version is anchoring — Robbins’ pre-speech gesture, Jordan’s free-throw ritual, and the accidental poverty anchors installed by a childhood of “we can’t afford that” — with the five-monkeys experiment standing for conditioning that outlives everyone who remembers the original punishment. The same substrate produces the rest of the cluster: thoughts arrive fully formed (ask for a blue dog and it appears), so you are the observer rather than the thinker, and Ironic Process Theory means suppression only rehearses; intuition is that machinery read back as pattern recognition delivered bodily, with the warning that a trauma response impersonates it; and micro-hesitation names the split second in which conditioning overrides the authentic move.
In: How To Reprogram Your Subconscious Mind (The Framework) · Subconscious Methods To Aid The Reprogramming Of Neural Pathways · The Conscious And Subconscious Mind: Everything You Need To Know · Internal Conflict and the Conscious-Subconscious Divide · Intuition and the Subconscious Mind: A Manual for Becoming Genuinely Intuitive · I Hacked My Brain to 10x My Income · The Forbidden Knowledge About How Your Brain Actually Works · In 1973, Three CEOs Disappeared After Exposing How Microhesitation Controls 90% of Human Behaviour
Neuroplasticity, myelination and the mechanics of habit
Plasticity is insisted on as value-neutral — the brain reinforces whatever is repeated, so bad habits are the ones running on myelinated superhighways — and the pieces here take the mechanism apart layer by layer. Synaptic connection has to exist before myelin can wrap it, which produces a four-phase habit model: reps 1–50 are barely-there construction and the point at which most people quit mistaking building for failure, 50–200 strengthen, myelination begins past 200, automaticity follows; daily repetition is mandatory because untended synaptic change decays in 24–48 hours, and habits are built one at a time because the construction budget is finite. Underneath sits hardware — Eriksson and Gage’s 1998 confirmation of adult neurogenesis in the dentate gyrus, BDNF as “miracle-gro” released by aerobic exercise, cortisol as directly neurotoxic to the hippocampus, and the split that exercise makes new neurons while novel learning is what keeps them alive — and the anterior midcingulate cortex, which grows on resistance and atrophies on comfort, so the disciplined have more structure rather than more will. Two companion pieces draw the conclusion: discipline is a lie because willpower is a depleting pool, and motivation is kindling rather than the log — a specific “dark motivation” carries the early phase until the pathway carries itself. Kaizen supplies the philosophy for all of it, 1.01^365 = 37.78×, alongside kintsugi and wabi-sabi against perfectionism as a fear response and shu-ha-ri as the ladder from following the rule to becoming it.
In: Neuroplasticity: Rewiring Your Brain To Do Hard Things · Synaptic Plasticity: What’s Actually Happening When You Try to Change · Neurogenesis: Your Brain Is Not Finished Building Itself · The Anterior Midcingulate Cortex: Your Brain’s Discipline Center · Why Discipline is a Lie · The Real Reason Discipline Alone Never Works · 5 Japanese Philosophies That Changed My Life
Perception as construction: the filter, the lens and the narrator
Roughly eleven million bits of sensory data arrive each second and forty to fifty reach consciousness, so what you call reality is the residue after the reticular activating system — a brainstem gatekeeper tuned by whatever you have repeatedly signalled as important — has finished filtering. Identity follows from this as “memorised focus,” the person you have been rehearsing, and the sharpest line in the cluster is that most people are building prisons with their focus and calling the prison their circumstances. The filter’s priorities are evolutionary rather than benevolent: six relevance filters running physical threat, social threat, uncertain reward, novelty, emotional intensity and identity relevance, with neutral good news failing to trip any of them — hence a day 95% fine that the brain spends on the 5%, and a nervous system calibrated in childhood chaos that reads peace as danger. Belief then reaches back into the body: Turin’s 1996 saline injections producing 30–50% pain reduction through genuine endogenous opioid release, open-label placebo working even when the patient knows, and nocebo doing the same in reverse. The countermeasures are training rather than positivity — romanticising as deliberate reappraisal with raised medial prefrontal activity, reduced amygdala reactivity and lower cortisol, and the inner narrator handled as construction rather than noise: Broca’s area making inner speech neurologically real, rumination holding cortisol up, Kross’s distanced self-talk converting self-evaluation into coaching, and the rule that “I made a mistake” stays outside the self-concept where “I’m an idiot” does not.

Consciousness, free will and the permanent observer

The antidote offered is not another person but accumulated evidence — self-love as kept promises, discipline as its highest form, every broken commitment a data point telling the subconscious you cannot be relied on, since you cannot love someone you do not trust. Detachment is the companion move, shifting the nervous system out of threat-scanning so quality returns, and character-testing (the Honda Accord and the McDonald’s suggestion) is the practical one, removing the resource signal to see who is there for it. Heartbreak is defended as a forced awakening with a genuine dopamine withdrawal on the other side of it, and friendship gets the longest treatment: a friendship recession, most friendships exposed as shared addictions that collapse when the routine is removed, the proximity trap of school, synchronised emotion mistaken for intimacy, Aristotle’s utility, pleasure and virtue with only the last surviving changed circumstances, self-expansion theory redrawing where you end and someone else begins, and the line the piece turns on — friends validate your identity while acquaintances validate your habits.
In: Why Modern Relationships Collapse After 6 Months · The Psychology Behind Why People Cheat · How to Test Character Before You Fall in Love · Why You Need to Get Your Heart Broken at Least Once · The Psychology of Letting Go: How Detachment Rewires Your Brain · A Lack Of Purpose Leads To Romantic Obsessions · The Art Of A Good Friendship · The Psychology of Loneliness
The modern social condition
Performative authenticity is named as the most inauthentic act available — curating an authentic-looking self for approval — and the pieces on it describe people who have stopped experiencing their lives and started producing them, photographing the sunrise rather than watching it, until the gap between the performed and actual self becomes the source of the emptiness. The comparison trap is stated as an equation: everyone knows the highlight reel is fake and everyone compares their real life to everyone else’s fake one, producing universal inadequacy out of a universal lie, and the endpoint is identity as brand, where stripping the performance leaves nothing behind. COVID is treated as a natural experiment in every mechanism the corpus already uses: a threat that never resolved holding cortisol and norepinephrine elevated for months, social circuitry thinning through disuse the way any unused skill does, two years of half-face input measurably impairing emotion recognition in children mid-development, context collapse from one room being asked to serve as office, gym and bedroom, Zoom forcing conscious processing of cues that should be automatic, and anxiety disorders up 25% since 2020. The high-and-low-vibration piece is his clearest statement of method — measurable infrared and cardiac electromagnetic output, chakras mapping onto nerve plexuses, and co-regulation through the vagus nerve and mirror neurons as the real mechanism — landing on “what spirituality calls energy, psychology calls social and emotional contagion; the mechanism is real either way.” And the neurodivergence essay is the deliberate correction to his own enthusiasm: neuroplasticity says brains change, neurodiversity says they do not all start from the same place, normal is only the centre of a distribution, ADHD is an interest-based attention system rather than a broken one, and the trap is that rewiring demands sustained voluntary attention — the exact faculty the condition compromises, “like trying to fix a broken hand using only that hand.”
In: The Performative Epidemic: Why Everything Feels Fake Now · The Curated Life That’s Making You Miserable · The Lasting Neuropsychological Effects Of COVID-19 · The Difference Between High And Low Vibrational People · Neurodivergence: Why Your Brain Was Never Meant To Be Normal
Greek and Japanese philosophy, mortality and time
The test he applies to a philosophy is durability — a trend dates with its decade, a philosophy survives every empire after it — and the six Greek frameworks are introduced against Pericles, whose logically sound war plan met one unaccounted variable and killed a quarter of Athens. Cynicism carries the most weight and gets a piece of its own: Diogenes in his jar answering Alexander’s offer of anything with “stand out of my sunlight,” throwing away his cup after watching a child drink from cupped hands, and the conclusion that “the more you own, the more you’re owned by what you own,” with the ledger closed by Alexander dead at 32 leaving an empire and Diogenes at 90 leaving a philosophy still in use — plus the correction that ancient Cynicism was liberation through simplicity, nothing like the bitterness the modern word carries. Alongside it: Epicurus on death being nowhere we are, Stoicism’s dichotomy of control, Heraclitus on rebuilding daily, and Socratic examination as the classical form of auditing inherited belief. Mortality is done by arithmetic — roughly 700,000 lifetime hours cut to about 250,000 usable ones after sleep, childhood and old age — with terror management explaining why the brain suppresses the sum, Kant invoked for time as a frame we bring rather than find, sunlight eight minutes old and starlight from things that no longer exist, the twin paradox with its actual evidence base in atomic clocks and particle decay, temporal discounting explaining why the future self is “a character in a story you’re telling yourself,” and the hedonic treadmill closing the other end with lottery winners and people who lost the use of their legs both back near baseline in about eighteen months. The residue is practical: memento mori and mono no aware presented as tools for waking up rather than dread, felt duration as memory density so that a life optimised for routine comfort disappears in retrospect, Camus’ Sisyphus for the peace available inside struggle, and Icarus reread — the source of the pen name — as a prisoner for whom flying too high was the free choice and the labyrinth was the cage.
In: 6 Greek Philosophies That Still Run Circles Around Modern Advice · How A Man With Nothing Became Wealthier Than Emperors · How To Find Peace In Struggle · Unfortunately, The Clock is Ticking · You’re Going To Run Out Of Time Before You Run Out Of Excuses · How to Make Your Life Feel Longer Without Living Longer · Would You Rather Live in a Cage or Die Free
Meaning, belief and freedom
Nihilism is treated as intellectual cowardice rather than a position — the philosophy adopted after the failure, giving inaction a costume — while granting that cosmic indifference is true and arguing it says nothing about whether effort, mastery or connection produce meaning; the existentialist answer is to construct it anyway, and the piece notes that quitting has a philosophy while finishing only has a practice. The essay he says he was afraid to write is the most honest in the corpus, running Sisyphus, terror management theory and Frankl’s insistence that meaning is made rather than found, and ending in engagement with the uncertainty rather than an answer — while noting purpose is physically measurable in cortisol, immune function and lifespan. Belief itself is presented as structural: nobody knows what happens after death and billions organise a life around their answer, secular people hold unprovable beliefs about success and worth as rigidly as any doctrine, beliefs become neural patterns through repetition, and challenging a core one triggers the threat response reserved for physical danger. The fine-tuning piece pushes furthest — odds around one in 10^120, DNA as information, consciousness unlocated in tissue — and the wiki files it as theological philosophy rather than neuroscience; synchronicity gets a similarly personal treatment, held as meditation rather than argument. The constructive half insists purpose is built rather than discovered, since a prediction machine can only learn from actual movement, with a validation test attached — would you still do this if nobody ever knew — and freedom is decomposed into physical, mental, financial and spiritual domains, cages built from perceptual narrowing where the brain stops generating options it has learned are not for you, and real freedom named as responsibility with nobody left to blame.

index.title: Symposium
index.content:
Symposium

A self-growing research wiki. Each section is a field under study; each section is compiled from named sources and credits the authors who wrote them.

The method is the same in every section: read the primary material, break it into concepts and entities, cross-link everything, and let the map get denser as more is read. Every claim traces back to a source, and every source traces back to an author.

Sections























SectionSubjectAuthorsBuilt fromPsychology, Neuroscience & Self-MasteryHow the mind runs on autopilot, and how the hardware is reprogrammedixcarus209 sources → 263 pagesMachine LearningHow machines learn from data — architectures, training, evaluation, and the systems built on them—28 sources → 46 pages
309 pages: 163 entities · 126 concepts · 16 topics · 4 synthesis reports.
Each section keeps its own hub, its own concept and entity pages, and its own source corpus. A new field is a new section — it does not disturb the existing ones.

Authors
Credit is computed, not declared: every page lists the authors of the sources it was built from, so attribution stays correct as the wiki grows.
→ All authors















AuthorSourcesSectionsixcarus209Psychology, Neuroscience & Self-Mastery

How to read this wiki
Start with a section hub. It carries the thesis, the domain map, and the way the field hangs together.
Then follow the concepts. Concept and entity pages are the substance — each synthesises several sources into one mechanism or idea, and links out to everything adjacent.
Sources sit underneath. Every section has a full source corpus, deliberately kept out of the sidebar so the ideas stay in front and the reading list stays behind. Sources remain fully linked, searchable, and one click away from any page that cites them — each section’s hub links to its complete list.
Keep what you read. Concept, topic and synthesis pages carry inline [!card] prompts next to the claims they test — a collapsed question you can answer before you reveal it. Enrol a page, a topic or a whole section, and review runs them back at you over expanding intervals.
Cards live on the pages themselves, never here or on review. To see one, open a page that carries them — cortisol and nervous-system-states are dense with them — or turn the whole feature on from the mortarboard in the toolbar, which is off until you ask for it.
See your route through the wiki. The reading map shows the pages you have read, how they connect, and where each field opens up next. It stays in this browser and does not send your reading history anywhere.

map.title: Reading Map

Reading Map
This is a map of the wiki’s ideas, rather than a card schedule. A page becomes seen when you arrive there and read once you have spent enough visible time with most of its prose. The map uses those signals only in this browser; nothing about your route is sent anywhere.
The circles are pages. Lines are the links that connect them; the brighter route is the last ninety days of your reading. A ring marks an unread page one link away from something you have read. Hover or focus a circle to name it, then open it to continue reading. The table below keeps the three field measures together: explored weights the pages a field connects to most, connected counts links whose two pages you have read, and pages is the plain count.
Choose a field above the map to look closely at it. Section hubs link here already filtered to their own field.
With JavaScript unavailable this remains a description of the map; the reader-specific view needs the record kept in your browser.
Your reading map and card schedule live only in this browser. Export or import
both together from Review if they matter to you. Clearing site data
loses them; on iPhone, install the site to keep them through a week away.

Review
Spaced repetition over the pages you have enrolled. Cards are written into the
prose as [!card] callouts, next to the claim they test — so a card is always
answerable from a page that already carries sources:, and inherits that page’s
attribution. There is nothing to memorise here that the wiki does not say.
Learning mode is off until you turn it on, from the mortarboard in the
toolbar, on any page. Off, a card is just a collapsible self-test in the prose and
nothing is scheduled. The caret beside it opens the settings.
Enrol from a page. Open anything carrying cards and press ☆ Learn this
page. A section hub enrols its whole section; a topic page enrols the concepts
beneath it. Nothing is enrolled by default. Enrolment decides what comes back to
you here; hard mode, below, decides what happens while you read.
Enrolling a section is safe. The wiki holds over a thousand cards, and one
section carries most of them — but enrolling it does not put a thousand cards in
front of you. New cards are introduced at a set rate, twenty a day by default, so
a section arrives over weeks rather than all at once. The control tells you how
many days it will take before you press it, and you can change the rate in the
settings. Cards already learned have their own daily ceiling.
Hard mode holds the page back. With it on, the prose below a card stays hidden
until you have answered that card, and the end of the page stays hidden until you
have remembered enough of them — 60% by default, and you can set the mark
yourself. Again still lets you read on; it just counts against the page, and
Hard counts as remembered. Miss the mark and the page tells you which ones to
take again. A card already scheduled from an earlier visit does not stop you, so
re-reading is uninterrupted until its cards fall due again.
Four grades: Again, Hard, Good, Easy. Each button shows the interval it buys,
so there is nothing to guess at. A new card is not scheduled in days straight
away — you see it again a minute later, then ten minutes later, and only then
does it move out to five days and start growing by roughly 2.3× a time. Getting
one wrong halves its interval and puts it back in a few minutes; it does not
throw away everything the card had earned. You can grade a card where it sits in
the prose, without coming here at all.
The queue takes a keyboard. Space or Enter reveals the answer; 1 2 3
4 grade it.
Progress lives in this browser. There is no account and no server — this is a
static site. Export it from the queue below if it matters to you, and import it
on another machine. Clearing site data loses it; on iPhone, install the site to
keep it through a week away.
Where the cards are
This page holds no cards of its own — it is a queue over the pages that do, and it
stays empty until you enrol something. Cards sit on concept, topic and synthesis
pages, next to the claim each one tests. Start from a hub and press ☆ Learn this
section, or open one of these and read down:

Psychology, Neuroscience & Self-Mastery — the section hub; enrols everything below it in one click
cortisol · nervous-system-states · sleep-optimization-protocol — dense concept pages, seven or eight cards each
The-Hijack-Map · The-Change-Architecture — synthesis reports

The queue appears below once the page loads. With JavaScript off, this page is
just prose and the cards remain what they are everywhere else: collapsible
self-tests you can answer without anything being recorded.

sections/machine-learning/concepts/agent.title: Agent Control Boundary
sections/machine-learning/concepts/agent.content:
Agent Control Boundary
The agent control boundary asks which transitions a human fixes in code and which a model chooses at run time. amans-ai-journal-primers-agents adopts the distinction between workflows, where models and tools follow predefined paths, and agents, where the model directs its own process.
flowchart LR
  W[Fixed workflow in code] --> M[Mixed control boundary]
  M --> A[Model-directed agent]
  W --> P[More predictability]
  A --> D[More adaptability]
  A --> F[More run-time decisions that can fail]
  G[Permissions verification and stopping rules] --> M



                  
                  What separates a workflow from an agent at the control boundary? 
                  
                

A workflow follows transitions fixed in code; an agent lets the model choose some transitions at run time.




                  
                  What is the cost of moving the control boundary toward the model? 
                  
                

More adaptability comes with another run-time decision that can fail.


The distinction is more useful as a continuum than a label. A system may let a model select a retrieval source while code fixes the evaluation loop; let it plan tasks while a human approves actions; or let it choose tools while deterministic guards set permissions and termination. Each shifted boundary adds adaptability and a new decision that can fail.
This reframes “how agentic is it?” into testable questions: Who selects the next action? Who decides the work is complete? Which actions require approval? What state survives between steps? What verifies the result? The answers determine the harness-engineering requirements and the appropriate evaluation, regardless of product naming.
Design implication
Use model-directed control where the environment is variable enough that fixed routes are brittle, and keep deterministic control where constraints and success conditions can be stated reliably. Autonomy is not itself capability; it is an allocation of decision rights.

sections/machine-learning/concepts/agent.title: Agent Protocol Layer
sections/machine-learning/concepts/agent.content:
Agent Protocol Layer
amans-ai-journal-primers-agents separates two interoperability boundaries. Model Context Protocol (MCP) standardizes how a model application discovers and connects to tools, resources, and prompts exposed by servers. Agent2Agent (A2A) addresses communication between agent systems through capability discovery, task lifecycle, messages, artifacts, and content negotiation.
flowchart TD
  P[Agent protocol layer] --> M[MCP]
  P --> A[A2A]
  M --> C[Application discovers tools resources and prompts]
  A --> G[Agent discovers capabilities and exchanges tasks]
  A --> T[Task lifecycle messages and artifacts]
  S[Protocol standardizes transport] --> B[Semantics permissions and trust still need design]



                  
                  What interoperability boundary does MCP standardize? 
                  
                

Application-to-capability access: discovering and connecting to tools, resources and prompts.




                  
                  How does A2A differ from MCP? 
                  
                

A2A coordinates tasks and artifacts between agent systems; MCP connects a model application to capabilities.


The distinction is functional:

MCP: application-to-capability access—what tools or data can this model-backed client use?
A2A: agent-to-agent collaboration—what can another agent do, how is a task exchanged, and how is progress represented?

They can coexist. An agent may use MCP-connected tools while participating in an A2A task with another agent. Traditional APIs still remain appropriate when a stable, explicitly coded integration is sufficient; a protocol layer earns its complexity when dynamic discovery or interoperability across implementations matters.
What protocols do not solve
A standardized connection does not validate the capability behind it, grant safe permissions, prevent prompt injection, or make task delegation correct. Authentication, authorization, data routing, privacy, schema design, and result verification remain harness-engineering and tool-interface-design concerns. Protocol compatibility is transport evidence, not competence evidence.
Related

sections/machine-learning/concepts/agent.title: Agentic Retrieval Routing
sections/machine-learning/concepts/agent.content:
Agentic Retrieval Routing
Vanilla Retrieval-Augmented-Generation usually places a fixed retrieval stage before generation. amans-ai-journal-primers-agents describes agentic RAG as moving retrieval decisions into the control loop: a model decides whether to retrieve, which source or specialist to call, how to reformulate a query, whether evidence is sufficient, and whether another hop is needed.
flowchart LR
  Q[Question arrives] --> D[Decide whether and where to retrieve]
  D --> R[Retrieve or reformulate]
  R --> E[Update state with evidence]
  E --> S[Check whether support is sufficient]
  S --> A[Synthesize supported answer]
  S --> D



                  
                  What makes retrieval agentic rather than a fixed RAG stage? 
                  
                

The model decides whether to retrieve, which source or query to use, and whether another hop is needed.




                  
                  When is deterministic retrieval preferable to agentic routing? 
                  
                

When one stable source and one search step reliably serve the task.


A single router can choose among vector search, web search, structured databases, or direct response. A multi-agent version delegates domains to specialists and aggregates their evidence. This makes retrieval conditional and adaptive, which is useful when questions require different stores or iterative evidence gathering.
The flexibility creates new failure surfaces. A model can skip retrieval when it is required, select the wrong source, loop across redundant searches, stop before contradictions are resolved, or spend more latency and tokens than a fixed pipeline. Routing quality, evidence coverage, termination, and citation fidelity must therefore be evaluated independently of answer fluency.
Design implication
Agentic routing is justified when retrieval needs vary meaningfully across queries. When one stable source and one search step serve the task, a deterministic pipeline is simpler and easier to test. This is an instance of the agent-control-boundary: delegate only the retrieval decisions whose variability earns model-directed control.

sections/machine-learning/concepts/backp.title: Backpropagation
sections/machine-learning/concepts/backp.content:
Backpropagation
An efficient application of the chain rule that computes gradients through a composed computational graph. It is distinct from gradient-descent: backpropagation supplies derivatives, while an optimizer decides how to use them to update parameters.
flowchart TD
  C[Cost, from the output against the label] --> N[Each output neuron records the nudge it wants]
  N --> S[Conflicting wishes summed into one desired change]
  S --> W[Adjust each weight in proportion to its incoming activation]
  S --> B[Adjust each bias directly]
  S --> A[Record what is wished of the previous activations]
  A --> N
  W --> G[Per-example derivatives]
  B --> G
  G --> M[Averaged over a mini-batch — the gradient]
  M --> D[Handed to gradient descent as the step direction]



                  
                  What exactly does backpropagation compute? 
                  
                

Gradients through the network’s composed operations. Backpropagation supplies derivatives; an optimizer such as gradient descent decides how those derivatives update parameters.


Two of Sanderson’s chapters cover it twice on purpose: backpropagation-really-doing-3blue1brown with “a complete disregard for notation,” then backpropagation-calculus-3blue1brown in chain-rule form, so the symbols arrive as articulation of something already understood “rather than acting as a code to be decrypted.”
Read a gradient component as sensitivity
This is the reframing that makes 13,002 dimensions thinkable. If one weight’s component is 3.2 and another’s is 0.1, then the cost is 32 times more sensitive to the first: the same wiggle changes the cost 32× as much. Direction matters less than the relative magnitudes, which rank the weights by, in Sanderson’s phrase, bang for your buck.


                  
                  What does a large gradient component mean? 
                  
                

The cost is proportionally more sensitive to that weight — a component of 3.2 against 0.1 means the same wiggle moves the cost 32× as much.


The intuitive derivation
Only three levers can raise one neuron’s activation — increase its bias, increase its weights, or change the activations feeding it. The bias is simplest because its effect on the weighted sum is constant. The other two produce a symmetry:

adjust each weight in proportion to its incoming activation
adjust each desired activation in proportion to its weight



                  
                  Which three levers can raise a neuron's activation? 
                  
                

Its bias, its incoming weights, and the activations feeding it. The bias is the simplest because its effect on the weighted sum is constant.




                  
                  Why is a weight adjusted in proportion to its incoming activation? 
                  
                

Because that activation is how much the weight actually moves the sum — formally ∂z/∂w = a. A weight attached to a barely-active neuron has little leverage over the output.


Activations cannot be set directly, so you record what is wished for. Every output neuron issues its own desired nudge to the previous layer, scaled by how wrong it is; these conflict, so you sum them into one desired change and recurse on the weights and biases that produced those activations. That recursion is the “backward.”


                  
                  What is the "backward" in backpropagation actually doing? 
                  
                

Propagating wishes. Activations cannot be set directly, so each output neuron records the nudge it wants from the previous layer; the conflicting wishes are summed and the procedure recurses onto the weights and biases that produced them.


Hebbian theory is visible in the formula
The largest weight increases happen between neurons that are most active and neurons you want to become more active — “neurons that fire together wire together.” backpropagation-calculus-3blue1brown shows exactly where it lives: ∂z⁽ᴸ⁾/∂w⁽ᴸ⁾ = a⁽ᴸ⁻¹⁾, so a weight matters more when the previous neuron is more active. Sanderson names the limit of the analogy himself — an untrained network is not “thinking” about a 2; the training label hardcodes what it should be thinking.
The calculus, on one neuron per layer
With z⁽ᴸ⁾ = w⁽ᴸ⁾a⁽ᴸ⁻¹⁾ + b⁽ᴸ⁾ and a⁽ᴸ⁾ = σ(z⁽ᴸ⁾):

∂C₀/∂w⁽ᴸ⁾ = a⁽ᴸ⁻¹⁾ · σ′(z⁽ᴸ⁾) · 2(a⁽ᴸ⁾ − y)

The bias case is identical with the first factor replaced by 1, since ∂z⁽ᴸ⁾/∂b⁽ᴸ⁾ = 1. Going further back multiplies in ∂z⁽ᴸ⁾/∂a⁽ᴸ⁻¹⁾ = w⁽ᴸ⁾ and repeats.
Real layer widths change exactly one thing. Index the layers by j and k and the weight derivative is the same three-factor product. What changes is the derivative with respect to a previous activation: that neuron influences the cost through every neuron in the next layer, so the expression becomes a sum over those paths of influence.


                  
                  What is the only thing that changes when layers are wider than one neuron? 
                  
                

The derivative with respect to a previous activation becomes a sum over paths of influence, because that neuron reaches the cost through every neuron in the next layer. The weight derivative is the same three-factor product.


Averaging across examples is an outer step
Backpropagation can compute the gradient of one example’s loss or of an aggregated batch loss. If C = (1/n)Σ Cₖ, linearity makes ∂C/∂w = (1/n)Σ ∂Cₖ/∂w. A per-example derivative is therefore a valid gradient component for that example; it is simply not the full-dataset empirical-risk gradient. Sanderson illustrates the distinction by noting that optimizing only one image of a 2 would encourage classifying everything as a 2.


                  
                  What goes wrong if a step follows the wishes of a single training example? 
                  
                

That example wants only its own label. Followed alone, the incentive is to classify everything as a 2 — the gradient is the average over examples for a reason.


Since averaging over every example per step is unaffordable, practice uses mini-batches of, say, 100 — worse gradient estimates taken far more often. Sanderson’s image: “a drunk man stumbling aimlessly down a hill but taking quick steps rather than a carefully calculating man who takes slow, deliberate steps.” That is stochastic gradient descent, catalogued as a variant in gradient-descent.
Scale changes nothing about the algorithm
large-language-models-explained-briefly-3blue1brown applies the same chain-rule procedure to models with hundreds of billions of parameters: predict a withheld next token, compare the distribution with the target, and propagate the loss gradient backward. The principle from the digit classifier is unchanged, while the graph, parameter count, batching, and distributed implementation are much larger.


                  
                  What does a mini-batch trade away, and what does it buy? 
                  
                

It trades gradient accuracy for step frequency — worse estimates taken far more often. Sanderson’s image is a drunk man stumbling downhill quickly against a careful man taking slow deliberate steps.


What to actually take away
Sanderson is explicit that the formulas are a library’s problem: “the most important and generalizable understanding here is how you can reason about the sensitivity of one variable to another by breaking down the chain of dependencies.”

sections/machine-learning/concepts/bias-.title: Bias/Variance Tradeoff
sections/machine-learning/concepts/bias-.content:
Bias/Variance Tradeoff
Bias is the gap between a model’s expected prediction and the truth. Variance is how much its prediction moves when the training data changes. Stated at its simplest, in vip-cheatsheet-machine-learning-tips-tricks: the simpler the model the higher the bias, the more complex the model the higher the variance.
flowchart LR
  T[Compare training error against test error] --> U[Training error high and close to test]
  T --> J[Training error slightly below test]
  T --> O[Training error much lower than test]
  U --> UB[High bias — underfitting]
  J --> JR[Fitted]
  O --> OV[High variance — overfitting]
  UB --> UR[Complexify, add features, train longer]
  OV --> OR[Regularise with LASSO, Ridge or Elastic Net, or add data]

Diagnosis by symptom
The most useful thing in the cheatsheet is a table that turns an abstraction into a decision procedure:



































UnderfittingJust rightOverfittingTraining errorHigh—LowTrain vs. testClose to test errorSlightly lower than testMuch lower than testVerdictHigh bias—High varianceRemedyComplexify the model, add features, train longer—Regularise, get more data
The diagnostic is the relationship between the two errors, not either number alone. A low training error means nothing by itself; a training error much below test error is the signature of variance.


                  
                  Why is a low training error uninformative on its own? 
                  
                

Because the diagnosis lives in the gap. Low training error close to test error is a fitted model; low training error far below test error is overfitting. The same number means opposite things depending on the pair.




                  
                  A model has high training error close to its test error. What is wrong and what fixes it? 
                  
                

High bias — it is underfitting. The remedy is more capacity: complexify the model, add features, train longer. Regularising or adding data would make it worse.


Regularisation is the variance instrument
Not a separate technique but the direct response to high variance, with three standard forms:

LASSO — adds λ‖θ‖₁. Shrinks coefficients to exactly zero, so it doubles as variable selection.
Ridge — adds λ‖θ‖²₂. Makes coefficients smaller without zeroing them.
Elastic Net — λ[(1−α)‖θ‖₁ + α‖θ‖²₂], trading variable selection against small coefficients.



                  
                  Why does LASSO double as variable selection where Ridge does not? 
                  
                

The L1 penalty shrinks coefficients to exactly zero, which drops those variables from the model. Ridge’s squared penalty makes coefficients small but never removes them.


The same knob elsewhere
k-nearest neighbours. vip-cheatsheet-supervised-learning states it directly: the higher k, the higher the bias and the lower the variance. One hyperparameter, the whole tradeoff.


                  
                  Which way does k move bias and variance in k-nearest neighbours? 
                  
                

Higher k means higher bias and lower variance — averaging over more neighbours smooths the prediction. One hyperparameter spans the whole tradeoff.


Dropout and batch normalisation. vip-cheatsheet-deep-learning presents dropout as a device “meant at preventing overfitting” — a variance reducer that happens to be implemented as stochastic unit removal rather than as a penalty term.
Cross-validation exists because a single train/test split gives a noisy estimate of variance. k-fold averages the error over k folds precisely so the estimate does not depend too much on one arbitrary partition.


                  
                  What problem is k-fold cross-validation solving? 
                  
                

A single train/test split gives a noisy estimate, dependent on one arbitrary partition. Averaging the error over k folds stops the verdict from resting on where the split happened to fall.


Model-selection criteria. Mallow’s Cₚ, AIC, BIC and adjusted R² all penalise parameter count. They are the same intuition expressed as a scalar: complexity must pay for itself.


                  
                  What single intuition do Mallow's Cₚ, AIC, BIC and adjusted R² share? 
                  
                

That complexity must pay for itself. Each penalises parameter count, so an added parameter only improves the criterion if it buys more fit than it costs.


Where the estimator vocabulary comes from
super-vip-cheatsheet-machine-learning supplies in §5.1.5 what the other sheets assume — bias of an estimator, sample mean and variance, the central limit theorem, confidence intervals. estimation-uncertainty keeps two levels distinct: estimator bias is systematic error in an estimated quantity, while predictive bias is systematic error from a restricted model class. They share the logic of systematic deviation, but are not interchangeable definitions.

sections/machine-learning/concepts/class.title: Classification Error Trade-offs
sections/machine-learning/concepts/class.content:
Classification Error Trade-offs
Classification error trade-offs begin with four counts rather than one score:
true positives, true negatives, false positives, and false negatives. Metrics differ
because they choose different denominators and therefore preserve different failure
modes.
flowchart LR
  C[Confusion matrix] --> P[Precision: TP / predicted positive]
  C --> R[Recall: TP / actual positive]
  C --> S[Specificity: TN / actual negative]
  C --> N[NPV: TN / predicted negative]
  T[Decision threshold] --> C
  K[Application error costs] --> T

Accuracy treats both correct classes together and can look strong when a majority
class dominates. Precision and recall focus on the positive class. Raising a
decision threshold commonly reduces false positives and raises precision while
missing more positives and reducing recall; lowering it reverses the emphasis.


                  
                  Why should precision and recall be reported together? 
                  
                

A threshold can improve one by sacrificing the other. Reporting only one hides the operating point and therefore hides which error was made cheaper.


F₁ is the harmonic mean of precision and recall. It is useful only when that
particular balance matches the decision. It ignores true negatives and assumes
equal weighting unless generalised to Fβ, so a good F₁ does not settle an asymmetric
medical, safety, or moderation problem.
ROC and precision–recall curves retain performance across thresholds. Their value
still depends on class structure: the primer warns that precision–recall can be
misleading when the negative class is rare, just as accuracy is misleading in
common positive-minority settings.
Crosslinks

rank-aware-evaluation — classification at a cutoff differs from ranking quality

sections/machine-learning/concepts/compo.title: Component-Wise RAG Evaluation
sections/machine-learning/concepts/compo.content:
Component-Wise RAG Evaluation
An end-to-end answer score cannot locate a RAG failure. amans-ai-journal-primers-retrieval-augmented separates retrieval evidence from generation behaviour so ingestion, candidate discovery, reranking, and synthesis can be improved independently.
flowchart LR
  I[Ingestion] --> R[Candidate retrieval]
  R --> K[Reranking]
  K --> G[Generation]
  R --> C[Measure context precision and recall]
  G --> F[Measure groundedness and answer relevance]
  C --> D[Locate missing-evidence failures]
  F --> D[Locate synthesis failures]
  D --> O[Join component results to product outcome]



                  
                  Why can an end-to-end answer score not diagnose a RAG system? 
                  
                

It cannot tell whether evidence was missed during retrieval or mishandled during generation.




                  
                  What is the difference between context precision and context recall? 
                  
                

Precision asks how much retrieved material is relevant; recall asks how much required evidence was recovered.


Retrieval measures include context precision—how much retrieved material is relevant—and context recall—how much required evidence was recovered. Context relevance asks whether passages address the query. These require a reference set or judge and should be measured before generation can obscure what was available.
Generation measures include groundedness or faithfulness to retrieved evidence, answer relevance, semantic similarity, exact match, string presence, and entity recall. A faithful answer can be wrong because the retrieved source was wrong; a factually correct answer can be ungrounded because the model used parametric memory. Both distinctions matter.
Diagnostic matrix

low retrieval recall + poor answer: missing evidence;
high retrieval quality + poor groundedness: synthesis failure;
high groundedness + wrong answer: corpus or reference failure;
good component scores + poor product outcome: metric or task mismatch.

Component metrics should be joined to latency, cost, permissions, user outcome, and adversarial slices. Automated model judges can scale evaluation but become another fallible component.

sections/machine-learning/concepts/conte.title: Context Engineering
sections/machine-learning/concepts/conte.content:
Context Engineering
Deciding what a model sees on each call. ai-agents-depth-design-principles-engineering gives it a whole chapter on the grounds that context determines the upper limit of agent capability — the model cannot act on what was never put in front of it, so context is the binding constraint before model quality is.
flowchart TD
  X[Context — the observation space, and it holds the tool definitions] --> L[Sets the upper limit of agent capability]
  D[Dynamic prompts, agent skills, the status bar] --> X
  A[Attention made distance within the window free] --> W[The window itself is finite]
  W --> P[More relevant information exists than fits]
  P --> C1[Compression, when the trajectory outgrows the window]
  P --> C2[Retrieval from an external store]
  P --> C3[Memory hierarchies]
  K[Stable parts first, volatile parts last] --> KV[The KV cache survives across turns]
  KV --> LC[Lower latency and cost]



                  
                  Why is context the binding constraint before model quality is? 
                  
                

The model cannot act on what was never put in front of it. However capable the policy, its ceiling is set by what the context actually contains.


Context is the observation space
In Bojie Li’s mapping onto reinforcement learning, Agent = LLM + Context + Tools corresponds to policy + observation space + action space. Context is what the agent can perceive. Li flags one subtlety: because tool definitions live in the context, what the agent “sees” includes what it can do, so the eyes/hands metaphor leaks. The observation space contains a description of the action space.


                  
                  Where does the eyes/hands split between context and tools break down? 
                  
                

Tool definitions live in the context. So the observation space contains a description of the action space — what the agent sees includes what it can do.


The engineering, concretely

KV-cache-friendly design. Order the prompt so the stable parts come first and the volatile parts last, and the cache survives across turns. This is a latency and cost property produced entirely by prompt ordering — one of the clearest cases where an implementation detail of Transformer inference dictates application architecture.



                  
                  Why does prompt ordering affect latency and cost?
                  
                

The KV cache survives only up to the first change. Putting the stable parts first and the volatile parts last keeps the cached prefix valid across turns — an inference detail that dictates application architecture.



System prompt optimisation — prompt engineering, treated as one technique inside context engineering rather than as the whole subject.
Dynamic prompts and agent skills — assembling the context per call from what the task needs, instead of shipping one static prompt.
The agent status bar — injecting meta-information about the trajectory so the model can reason about where it is in a long task, not just what was said.



                  
                  What does an agent status bar give the model that the transcript alone does not? 
                  
                

Where it is in the task. The conversation records what was said; injected meta-information about the trajectory lets the model reason about its own progress through a long run.



Context compression — explicit strategies for when the trajectory outgrows the window, which it always eventually does.

Why it exists at all
Because the context window is finite, and every source in this section that touches agents runs into the same wall:

llm-powered-autonomous-agents-lillog names finite context length as its first limitation, and notes that vector stores extend reach but their representational power is weaker than full attention.
rag-vs-long-context treats retrieval and window capacity as complementary: retrieval saves tokens and isolates evidence, while long context preserves material a retriever might omit.
Context compression, retrieval, and memory hierarchies are three answers to one problem: more relevant information exists than fits.

Within retrieval, context quality begins before prompting. retrieval-chunking-boundary determines whether qualifications stay attached to claims, while component-wise-rag-evaluation distinguishes a context-selection failure from a generation failure.


                  
                  What single problem do compression, retrieval and memory hierarchies all answer? 
                  
                

That more relevant information exists than fits. Each is a different way of choosing what makes it into a finite window.


Seen that way, context engineering is long-term-dependency arriving at the application layer. Attention made distance within the window free and made the window itself the constraint; context engineering is the discipline of spending that budget well.


                  
                  What did attention do to the long-dependency problem rather than solve? 
                  
                

It moved it. Distance within the window became free, and the window itself became the constraint — so the problem reappears one layer up as how to spend a finite context budget.


Sources

ai-agents-depth-design-principles-engineering (primary — Ch. 2, and the RL mapping)
llm-powered-autonomous-agents-lillog (finite context as a named limitation)

sections/machine-learning/concepts/diffu.title: Diffusion Guidance
sections/machine-learning/concepts/diffu.content:
Diffusion Guidance
Diffusion guidance steers the reverse process toward a condition such as a class label or text representation. are-diffusion-models-lillog distinguishes two routes.
flowchart TD
  G[Steer the reverse process] --> C[Classifier guidance]
  G --> F[Classifier-free guidance]
  C --> S[Separate noisy-image classifier supplies a gradient]
  F --> M[One model learns conditional and unconditional predictions]
  S --> A[Stronger condition adherence]
  M --> A
  A --> T[Higher scale trades diversity for alignment and artifacts]



                  
                  How does classifier-free guidance avoid a separate classifier? 
                  
                

One model learns both conditional and unconditional predictions, whose difference steers sampling.




                  
                  What does a higher diffusion guidance scale trade away? 
                  
                

Diversity and sometimes artifact-free samples, in exchange for stronger condition adherence.


Classifier guidance uses the gradient of a separately trained noisy-image classifier to modify the unconditional reverse score. The classifier must operate across diffusion noise levels, and its gradient points sampling toward regions associated with the desired class.
Classifier-free guidance trains one model with and without the condition by sometimes dropping conditioning. At sampling time, conditional and unconditional predictions are combined; scaling their difference strengthens adherence to the condition without requiring a separate classifier.
The guidance scale is a tradeoff rather than a free quality knob. Stronger conditioning can improve prompt or class alignment while reducing diversity and producing artifacts or oversaturated samples. Unconditional and conditional branches must both be learned well enough for their difference to provide a useful direction.
Separation from generation speed
Guidance determines where the reverse trajectory is steered. Fewer-step samplers, distillation, consistency models, and latent diffusion determine how expensively that trajectory is traversed. A method can change one without solving the other.

sections/machine-learning/concepts/diffu.title: Diffusion Noise Prediction
sections/machine-learning/concepts/diffu.content:
Diffusion Noise Prediction
are-diffusion-models-lillog explains why a diffusion model can train without simulating every forward step. The forward Gaussian process has a closed form for sampling a corrupted (x_t) directly from clean data (x_0) at a chosen timestep. Training samples (t), adds known noise (\epsilon), and asks a network to predict that noise from (x_t) and (t).
flowchart LR
  X[Clean sample] --> N[Choose a timestep and add known noise]
  N --> C[Corrupted sample]
  C --> M[Network predicts the added noise]
  M --> L[Denoising loss compares predicted and known noise]
  L --> R[Learned reverse denoising direction]



                  
                  Why can diffusion training corrupt a clean sample at any chosen timestep directly? 
                  
                

The forward Gaussian process has a closed form, so earlier corruption steps need not be simulated.




                  
                  What target does the standard simplified diffusion objective predict? 
                  
                

The known noise added to the clean sample.


The original variational lower bound decomposes into a terminal term without learned parameters, Gaussian KL terms for intermediate reverse transitions, and a decoder term at the final step. Under the DDPM parameterization, the relevant mean-prediction terms can be rewritten as weighted denoising losses. The widely used simplified objective trains directly on squared error between sampled and predicted noise.
Predicting noise is a parameterization of the reverse process, not evidence that the model stores clean images or merely removes visible static. Across noise levels, the network estimates the direction needed to move a corrupted sample toward higher data density. This links DDPM training to noise-conditioned score estimation.
Boundary
Loss weighting, variance schedules, reverse variance, prediction target, and sampler alter behaviour. The simplified epsilon loss is practical and influential, but it is not the only diffusion objective and does not make all bound terms or modelling choices irrelevant.
